question: The median of the observations 20, 23, 25, 30, 20, 31, 32, 35, 20, 41, 42, 43, 20, 20 and 20 is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total number of observations (**n**) = **15** (which is an **odd number**).

Arrange in **ascending order**: 20, 20, 20, 20, 20, 20, 23, **25**, 30, 31, 32, 35, 41, 42, 43.

For odd **n**, **Median** = ((n + 1) ÷ 2)th observation.

**Median** = (16 ÷ 2)th = **8th term**.

Scanning the sorted list, the **8th term** is **25**.

**∴ The correct answer is 25.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given observations:** 20, 23, 25, 30, 20, 31, 32, 35, 20, 41, 42, 43, 20, 20, 20

**Formula Used:**

If **n** is **odd**: Median = Value of ((n + 1) ÷ 2)th term.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f53110b5f51efbf1347139f1357014739f82647cd8c62cc0c776c5de15a82e6c.png] 

⇒ **Step 1:** Arrange the data in **ascending order**:

20, 20, 20, 20, 20, 20, 23, 25, 30, 31, 32, 35, 41, 42, 43

⇒ **Step 2:** Count the **number of observations (n)**:

n = 15

⇒ **Step 3:** Calculate **Median position**:

Position = (15 + 1) ÷ 2 = 16 ÷ 2 = **8th term**

⇒ **Step 4:** Identify the **8th term** in the sorted list:

Sorted Data [8] = 25

**∴ The correct answer is 25.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Median for Even Data

If the number of observations (n) is **even**, the median is the **average** of the (n ÷ 2)th and ((n ÷ 2) + 1)th terms.

Mode of Data

The **mode** is the observation that appears **most frequently**. In the given set, the mode is 20 (appears 6 times).

Empirical Relationship

The relationship between central tendencies is given by: **Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean**.

Mean Calculation

The **Mean** is calculated as the **Sum of all observations** divided by the **total number** of observations (n).</p
